item.title: Implement TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter in ratelimit.py per SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py` (the module currently only has stubs). Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases; the tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics. Keep it dependency-free (standard library only) and commit your work."

Goal: implement `TokenBucket` and `KeyedLimiter` in `ratelimit.py` exactly as `SPEC.md` describes. The spec is the acceptance criteria.

Requirements to honour (all from SPEC.md):
- Time is read only through the injected `clock` callable (float seconds, monotonic). Default `time.monotonic`.
- TokenBucket: capacity > 0 and refill_per_sec > 0, else ValueError. Starts full. Fractional tokens allowed, tokens accrue continuously and never exceed capacity.
- try_acquire(n=1): all-or-nothing; n <= 0 or n > capacity raises ValueError; returns False without removing anything when short.
- available(): tokens after refill.
- wait_time(n=1): seconds until try_acquire(n) would succeed, 0.0 if now; does not consume; same ValueError rules.
- Clock going backwards: nothing changes (no tokens added or removed) until the clock passes the latest time already seen.
- KeyedLimiter(capacity, refill_per_sec, max_keys=1024, clock=time.monotonic): one independent TokenBucket per hashable key, created on first use. try_acquire(key, n=1) and wait_time(key, n=1) behave like bucket methods. At most max_keys buckets; on overflow evict the least recently used key first; try_acquire and wait_time both count as use; an evicted key returning starts full. max_keys < 1 raises ValueError, as do invalid capacity/refill_per_sec. len(limiter) = number of keys currently tracked.

Constraints: standard library only, no new dependencies. Keep functions under 60 lines, explicit data flow, assertions/validation at boundaries per the repo's coding rules. Add tests in `test_ratelimit.py` covering the edge cases above (clock going backwards, fractional refill, cap at capacity, n > capacity, LRU eviction order including wait_time counting as use, evicted key returns full, max_keys validation). Existing tests must still pass. Commit the work on the branch with a clear message; do not push.

model_reasons.implement: Single small module fully specified by SPEC.md; one author suffices. Standard review because edge-case errors could hide in a rate limiter.

evidence.caption: Before: original stubs, all 3 tests error

pr.body: Approach: TokenBucket refills lazily from the injected clock, capped at capacity; clock steps backwards are ignored until the latest seen time is passed. KeyedLimiter keeps an OrderedDict of key to TokenBucket, bounded by max_keys with LRU eviction; try_acquire and wait_time both count as use. n is validated before any key is created. Files: ratelimit.py, test_ratelimit.py. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v, 16/16 OK; py_compile ok (pyflakes not installed). Review: agt_01M8GGFS7203GTPKNSD287M7SX pass, no blocking findings. Follow-up nits: capacity=inf accepted; no direct test for KeyedLimiter.wait_time invalid n or backwards clock at keyed level.
pr.summary: Made rate limiting available: TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter in ratelimit.py. Now can limit per key with LRU eviction. Before: stubs raising NotImplementedError; now: 16 tests pass.
